source_review.notes: Checked current PostgreSQL 18 synchronous-commit, priority/quorum standby, replication statistics, remote-write/flush/apply behavior; current MySQL 8.4 asynchronous, semisynchronous plugin, acknowledgement-count, wait-point, timeout/fallback, and replication-thread behavior; and primary-backup, transaction-processing, and consensus foundations.

evidence: Defined local and remote acknowledgement times, order statistics, eligible set, threshold, acknowledged frontier, receive/write/flush/apply stages, priority/threshold policy, degraded mode, and commit ambiguity before use.
notation_and_syntax.notes: Acknowledgement, durability, application, visibility, election, promotion, and fencing evidence remain distinct.

evidence: Recomputed local 4 ms; ANY-1/2/3 remote-flush 8/23/60 ms; ANY-2 remote-apply 40 ms; priority r2+r3 flush 60 ms; Exercise 2 values 6, 10, 31, 28, and 90 ms; and asynchronous candidate gaps of 3 and 8 positions.
numerical_recomputation.notes: All latency values are labeled earliest finite-model times rather than production percentile predictions.

evidence: Reviewed T_success = max(T_L,T_(k)^A), priority maximum, acknowledgement monotonicity, durable-copy loss-exposure implication, strict-threshold availability predicate, and timeout indistinguishability argument.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: Latency derivation is explicitly a lower bound, while safety retains topology, history, integrity, promotion, and fencing premises.

evidence: Reviewed response loss, late acknowledgement, source/replica process and power cuts, shared failure domains, duplicate identities, slow priority members, replay stalls, full disks, membership changes, degraded mode, catch-up restoration, wrong candidate promotion, and stale-writer fencing.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: Timeout and cancellation never serve as proof of transaction abort.

evidence: Checked truthful stage acknowledgements, distinct eligible membership, configured threshold, source/remote durable evidence, explicit fallback epochs, visibility-aware reads, promotion coverage, and stable transaction identity; the executable fixture reproduced threshold decisions.
invariant_checking.notes: Replica count is not treated as failure-domain independence or consensus.

evidence: Reviewed order-statistic latency, pipeline causality, acknowledged-copy survival premises, availability/safety mode transition, and indistinguishable pre/post-commit timeout cuts.
proof_review.notes: Conditional zero-loss language is bounded to the stated durable-copy and failover model.

evidence: Audited asynchronous, synchronous, semisynchronous, local durable, received, written, flushed, applied, visible, eligible, degraded, ambiguous, promoted, elected, and fenced terminology.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: PostgreSQL and MySQL product labels are versioned and not generalized into universal guarantees.

evidence: CPython 3.14.4 reproduced the finite acknowledgement-threshold, priority, apply-stage, and duplicate-identity fixture on macOS 13.7.8 x86_64.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: The fixture does not implement a database, network, storage flush, failure detector, membership service, election, promotion, or fence.

conceptual_review.notes: Reviewed acknowledgement contracts, pipeline stages, priority and threshold membership, latency, loss exposure, timeout/fallback, ambiguity, read visibility, topology change, logical apply, degraded operation, and evidence.

practitioner_review.notes: Reviewed transaction classes, failure domains, latency tails, client idempotency/status lookup, automatic fallback hazards, admission control, catch-up, promotion eligibility, fencing, instrumentation, and deterministic fault cuts.

pedagogical_review.notes: The Level-II chapter derives acknowledgement latency and conditional durability from typed stages, supplies a passing finite model, ten distinct examples, and five progressive exercises with complete answers.

limitations: Internal source, mathematical, snippet, conceptual, practitioner, and pedagogical review only; no external database-vendor, storage, network, distributed-systems, security, reliability, or production review is claimed. Conclusions remain conditional on source and replica durability semantics, truthful authenticated acknowledgements, membership and failure-domain independence, history and integrity, transaction class, thresholds, timeouts and degraded policy, workload and latency distribution, client retry protocol, read visibility, promotion and fencing, implementation, configuration, and future version drift.
